intro: This is the code for your accordion, exactly as it will be pasted. Notice that the same text appears in several places: hover any value and every copy lights up.

parts.label: The whole accordion
parts.what: The outer box that holds every item. It gets a name (its `id`) so the items can say “we belong to this group”.
parts.how: Bootstrap's accordion script uses that shared name to make “only one open at a time” work: when one panel opens, it closes the other panels that name the same group.
parts.deep: The group's `id` is repeated as `data-bs-parent="#…"` on every panel. Remove it from a panel and that panel opens and closes on its own, ignoring the others.

parts.label: One item
parts.what: One title together with its hidden panel, kept as a pair.
parts.how: Adding or removing an item in the builder adds or removes a whole pair, with the names inside it kept in step for you.
parts.deep: `accordion-item` is a Bootstrap class. Our CSS removes its default border so the items look like plain links with an arrow.

parts.label: The heading
parts.what: Wraps the title in a real heading (`h3`), so screen readers can jump from title to title.
parts.how: The heading has its own `id`. The panel points back to it (`aria-labelledby`), so a screen reader announces the panel together with its title.
parts.deep: Using a real heading element rather than styled text keeps the page's structure correct for assistive technology.

parts.label: The title you click
parts.what: A real button, so it works with a mouse and with the keyboard (Tab to reach it, Enter or Space to open it).
parts.how: Three attributes make it work. `data-bs-toggle` says “I open and close something”. `data-bs-target` says which panel, by its `id`. `aria-expanded` tells screen readers whether it is open right now.
parts.deep: Bootstrap flips `aria-expanded` and the `collapsed` class each time it is clicked. The `collapsed` class is why the arrow points right when closed; our CSS rotates it when the class is removed.

parts.label: The title text
parts.what: Your title. It sits in its own `span` so our CSS can underline it, and remove the underline on hover.

parts.label: The hidden panel
parts.what: The part that opens and closes. It stays hidden until its button is clicked.
parts.how: It has an `id`, and its button's `data-bs-target` has the same text. That match is how a click finds its panel. If they differ by even one letter, clicking does nothing and there is no error message.
parts.deep: The `collapse` class hides it and Bootstrap adds `show` while it is open. `data-bs-parent` names the accordion, so opening this one closes the others.

parts.label: Where your content goes
parts.what: An empty slot. Build another block on its own tab, then paste its HTML in place of the comment.
parts.how: Anything works in here: text, a list, buttons, even another block.
parts.deep: `<!-- Content goes here -->` is only a placeholder comment. Delete it when you paste your content.

attributes.data-bs-target: Names the panel this button opens. The `#` means “the element with this id”. It has to match the panel's `id` exactly: one wrong letter and the button silently does nothing.
attributes.data-bs-parent: Names the accordion this panel belongs to, so that opening this panel closes the others.
attributes.data-bs-toggle: Tells Bootstrap's script “this button opens and closes something”. `collapse` is the kind of opening.
attributes.aria-expanded: Tells screen readers whether the panel is open. Bootstrap changes it for you each click.
attributes.aria-controls: Tells screen readers which panel this button controls.
attributes.aria-labelledby: Tells screen readers that this panel is described by its heading.
